papers.title: Influence of laser shock peening on the residual strains and stresses in additively manufactured TC4
papers.abstract: Additively manufactured materials possess significant heterogeneities and anisotropies of stiffness and strength properties between the growth and transverse directions. Residual stresses induced by the fabrication and processing stages are critical to the service life of these materials. In this work, an experimental study of the residual stress fields was conducted in samples cut from additively manufactured titanium alloy TC4. The depth profiles of residual elastic strains for various regimes of laser impact treatment were obtained on elementary samples in the form of rectangular plates of 100´20´5 mm. Five treatment regimes were studied by varying the laser power density, the spot shape, and the percentage of overlap. The dependence of relief strains and residual stress levels on the laser energy density was obtained for two laser spot shapes: a 1´1 mm square and a 2 mm diameter circle. The numerical model, validated against experimental data for both as-built and laser-peened states, provides a reliable tool for analyzing the residual stresses and strain in additively manufactured components.

papers.title: Effect of Low-Pressure Gas Oxynitriding on the Microstructural Evolution and Wear Resistance of Ti-6Al-4V Alloy
papers.abstract: A Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy exhibits low hardness and poor wear resistance under sliding contact. This study evaluates the effect of low-pressure gas oxynitriding (LPON) followed by low-temperature oxidation on its microstructure and tribological performance. Specimens were nitrided at 1000 °C for 100 min, then oxidized at 450–600 °C for 120 min. Microstructural and phase changes were characterized by SEM and XRD; surface roughness, hardness, and wear were assessed using 3D laser scanning microscopy, microhardness profiling, and pin-on-disk tests under 2 N and 4 N loads. XRD revealed TiN, Ti2N, Ti2AlN, and TiO2 phases, with oxidation temperature governing TiN grain growth and nitride-to-oxide transformation. Oxidation at 500–550 °C formed a dense TiO2-rich layer over a stable TiN/Ti2N substrate, achieving hardness up to ~670 HV0.025 and the lowest wear volume. At low load (2 N), nitriding alone provided the highest wear resistance, while at higher load (4 N), oxidation yielded only slight improvement due to oxide embrittlement. Excessive oxidation at 600 °C increased roughness, induced spallation, and reduced wear resistance. The optimal condition (550 °C) offered synergistic protection from nitrides and stable oxides, enhancing load-bearing capacity. Overall, duplex nitriding–oxidation is most effective for low-to-moderate load applications, with potential use in biomedical implants, aerospace fasteners, and precision components.

summary_zh.motivation: Ti-6Al-4V合金硬度低、耐磨性差，需通过表面处理改善。

summary_zh.validation: 通过SEM、XRD、显微硬度、销盘磨损试验验证。

summary_en.motivation: Ti-6Al-4V alloy suffers from low hardness and poor wear resistance under sliding contact, necessitating surface modification.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V was treated by low-pressure gas oxynitriding (1000°C nitriding) followed by low-temperature oxidation (450–600°C); microstructure, hardness, and wear were evaluated.
summary_en.result: Oxidation at 550°C produced a dense TiO₂ layer over a TiN/Ti₂N substrate, achieving ~670 HV0.025 hardness and minimal wear volume.
summary_en.validation: Characterization via SEM, XRD, microhardness profiling, and pin-on-disk wear testing.
